posts:
An AI startup demands transparency from the very studios suing it for copyright infringement.

Midjourney wants Hollywood...
Evidence: fair use defense, legal discovery, industry custom
#Aletheia #AI

Midjourney claims it wants to expose industry custom to prove that studios also use generative AI internally, supporting fair use.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, -0.5) — Lesser Good

Midjourney is using aggressive legal discovery as a leverage tactic to force studios into a settlement by threatening their secrets.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, +0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Using legal discovery to expose competitor secrets rather than addressing the core copyright claim.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (R_net: 2.8, Uncertainty z: 2)
In an ongoing copyright lawsuit, Midjourney is asking a judge to compel Disney, Universal, and Warner Bros. to reveal their internal AI usage.

The Bright Side:
Exposing how major studios use AI internally could bring much-needed transparency to the entertainment industry's labor practices.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing industry custom (WHAT) with legal permission (WHO). Just because studios experiment with AI doesn't mean unlicensed scraping is legal.

Social Physics Analysis:
Midjourney projects its own copyright violations onto the plaintiffs, using a pretext of industry transparency to distract from its unauthorized training practices.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. Legal leverage overrides fair use principles.

The Unavoidable Truth: Both sides want to use AI while protecting their own intellectual property.

The Unavoidable Lie: This discovery request is purely about fair use defense.

Alethekanon:
This is a classic counter-offensive legal strategy. By threatening to expose the studios' internal AI experiments, Midjourney seeks to force a settlement.

Awwthekanon:
It's sad to see creative tools and art reduced to a massive corporate chess game where artists' original works are just bargaining chips.

Brothekanon:
Midjourney is basically saying, 'I know you guys are using AI in the back room too, so let's all just get along or I'll spill the tea.'
